brief: A shelf unit rated to hold 50 kg of books, with two drawers.

requirements.requirement: Shelf unit rated to hold 50 kg of books
requirements.evidence: Four-cell block with two-compartment bins as shelves was built, but the configurator has no load model; the 50 kg rating depends on material and print, which I cannot verify. Not claimed.
Two drawer-frame notches (hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf) placed at (-1,1,0) and (0,-1,0). The tools offered no separate drawer part for notch sites, so drawer fronts and sliding action are not confirmed.

finish.summary: Built a four-cell hex storage block at level 0: full bases at (-1,0), (0,0), (1,0), (0,1), each holding a two-compartment bin as an open shelf, with two drawer-frame notches at (-1,1) and (0,-1). Caps close the open faces and joints are bolted (lockJoints). check_build is clean with meshClash clear. The 50 kg rating cannot be verified: the configurator checks fit and collisions only, and load capacity depends on the printed material and print settings, which I cannot see. The drawers are frame notches; I could not add separate drawer fronts through the tools, so the drawer function is only partly confirmed.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
